Macaria Francisco (Macaria) and Marcos Averia contracted marriage which bore six issues, namely: Gregorio, Teresa, Domingo, Angel, Felipe and Felimon.
Family history; issues means children here.
Macaria was widowed and she contracted a second marriage with Roberto Romero (Romero) which bore no issue.
Romero died on February 28, 1968, leaving three adjoining residential lots located at Sampaloc, Manila.
In a Deed of Extrajudicial Partition and Summary Settlement of the Estate of Romero, the house and lot containing 150 square meters at 725 Extremadura Street, Sampaloc was apportioned to Macaria.
Transfer Certificate of Title (TCT) No. 93310 covering the Extremadura property was accordingly issued in the name of Macaria.

Alleging that fraud was employed by her co-heirs in the partition of the estate of Romero, Macaria filed on June 1, 1970 an action for annulment of title and damages before the Court of First Instance of Manila against her co-heirs Domingo Viray, et al., docketed as Civil Case No. 79955.
Earlier litigation; not an issue framed for this petition.

The case was pending litigation for about ten years until the decision of the Court of Appeals which adjudged Macaria as entitled to an additional 30 square meters of the estate of Romero became final and executory.
Reports the outcome of an earlier proceeding.
Macaria’s son Gregorio and his family and daughter Teresa’s family lived with her at Extremadura until her death on March 28, 1983.

Close to six years after Macaria’s demise or on January 19, 1989, her children Domingo, Angel and Felipe, along with Susan Pelayo vda. de Averia (widow of Macaria’s deceased son Felimon), filed before the Regional Trial Court (RTC) of Manila a complaint against their brother Gregorio and niece Sylvanna Vergara “representing her absentee mother” Teresa Averia, for judicial partition of the Extremadura property inclusive of the 30 square meters judicially awarded.
One complete sentence across the page break.

Gregorio and Sylvanna further countered that the plaintiff Domingo sold and assigned to the spouses Gregorio and Agripina his one sixth (1/6) share in the remaining ½ portion of the Extremadura property.
Factual allegation of a transaction; not a judicial holding.
During the pendency of the case or on June 7, 1989, Macaria’s son Felipe executed a Waiver-Affidavit waiving his “share” in the property subject of litigation in favor of his co-heirs.
Both parties are hereby ordered to shoulder their respective expenses for attorney’s fees and litigation costs.
Quoted RTC disposition reported as procedural history.

In reversing the trial court, the appellate court, noting that the alleged transfers made by Macaria and Domingo in favor of Gregorio were bereft of any written memoranda, held that it was error for the trial court to rely solely on the evidence adduced by the defendants consisting of the testimonies of Gregorio, Veronica Bautista, Sylvanna Vergara Clutario, Atty. Mario C. R. Domingo, Felimon Dagondon and Gregorio Averia, Jr.
Reports the appellate ruling that the Supreme Court reviews.
[T]he alleged conveyances purportedly made by Macaria Francisco and plaintiff-appellant Domingo Averia are unenforceable as the requirements under the Statute of Frauds have not been complied with.
Quoted CA reasoning subsequently rejected; not the current Supreme Court holding.

The case is remanded to the court a quo which is directed to effect the partition of the subject property or if not possible, sell the entire lot and distribute the proceeds of the sale based on equal shares among the children of the late Macaria Francisco after debts of the said deceased are paid or settled pursuant to Article 1078 of the Civil Code.
Quoted CA disposition; distinguishes earlier disposition from current RULING.

THE COURT OF APPEALS (SECOND DIVISION) ERRED IN ITS FINDING THAT THERE WAS NO SALE OF ONE-HALF (½) OF THE DECEASED MACARIA F. AVERIA’S INTEREST AND OWNERSHIP OVER THE SUBJECT PROPERTY IN FAVOR OF PETITIONER GREGORIO F. AVERIA.
First assignment of error in the present Supreme Court petition: alleged sale of Macaria’s half interest.

THE COURT OF APPEALS (SECOND DIVISION) ERRED IN ITS FINDING THAT THE RECEPTION OF PAROL EVIDENCE TO THE EFFECT THAT RESPONDENT DOMINGO AVERIA HAD ALREADY SOLD HIS ONE SIXTH (1/6) SHARE IN THE SUBJECT PROPERTY IN FAVOR OF PETITIONER GREGORIO AVERIA IS NOT IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW.
Second assignment of error in the present petition: legality of receiving parol evidence of Domingo’s sale.

With respect to the application by the appellate court of the Statute of Frauds, petitioners contend that the same refers only to purely executory contracts and not to partially or completely executed contracts as in the instant case.
Supporting argument for inapplicability of the statute; alternative ISSUE if codebook treats this as independent issue framing, or FACT under party-argument convention.

The finding of the CA that the testimonies of petitioners’ witnesses were timely objected to by respondents is not, petitioners insist, borne out in the records of the case except with respect to the testimony of Gregorio.
Specifically challenges the CA finding of timely objections; alternative FACT as reported procedural assertion rather than separate issue framing.
Current Supreme Court answer; singular petitioner retained as printed.

Indeed, except for the testimony of petitioner Gregorio bearing on the verbal sale to him by Macaria of the property, the testimonies of petitioners’ witnesses Sylvanna Vergara Clutario and Flora Lazaro Rivera bearing on the same matter were not objected to by respondents.
Current Court evaluates the evidentiary record supporting its answer.
Following Article 1405 of the Civil Code, the contracts which infringed the Statute of Frauds were ratified by the failure to object to the presentation of parol evidence, hence, enforceable.

Contrary then to the finding of the CA, the admission of parol evidence upon which the trial court anchored its decision in favor of respondents is not irregular and is not foreclosed by Article 1405.
Printed respondents appears inconsistent with the RTC ruling favoring petitioners; wording retained without correction.
In any event, the Statute of Frauds applies only to executory contracts and not to contracts which are either partially or totally performed.
Rule expressly applied by the current Court.

In the case at bar, petitioners claimed that there was total performance of the contracts, full payment of the objects thereof having already been made and the vendee Gregorio having, even after Macaria’s death in 1983, continued to occupy the property until and after the filing on January 19, 1989 of the complaint subject of the case at bar as in fact he is still occupying it.
Reports petitioners’ claimed payment and possession within the Court’s analysis; alternative RULING if treated as adopted factual application.
In proving the fact of partial or total performance, oral evidence may be received as what the trial court in the case at bar did.
However it is not enough for a party to allege partial performance in order to render the Statute of Frauds inapplicable; such partial performance must be duly proved.
Tolentino passage expressly adopted to explain the applicable proof requirement.
But neither is such party required to establish such partial performance by documentary proof before he could have the opportunity to introduce oral testimony on the transaction.
The partial performance may be proved by either documentary or oral evidence.
The testimonies of petitioners’ witnesses being credible and straightforward, the trial court did not err in giving them credence.
Supreme Court endorses the trial court’s credibility assessment.
The testimony of Sylvana Vergara Clutario, daughter of Teresa, in fact was more than sufficient to prove the conveyance of half of the subject property by Macaria to Gregorio.
Supreme Court conclusion about sufficiency of evidence.
Are you the same Sylvana Vergara representing the defendant Teresa Averia in this case?
Witness-identification question, not a disputed legal question; alternative FACT if codebook groups all evidentiary examination as FACT.
Because of her embarrassment, she told them that one half (½) of the House and Lot will be given to the couple to cover the expenses of the case.
Quoted witness account of the consideration for the conveyance.
Her testimony was against the interest of her mother Teresa whom she represented, her mother being also an heir of Macaria.
Current Court explains why testimony is credible.
If the transfer by Macaria to Gregorio of ½ of the property is upheld as valid and enforceable, then the share of the other heirs including Sylvanna’s mother would considerably be reduced.
Explains adverse interest as a credibility reason; not an ISSUE merely because it uses a conditional.

As to the sale of Domingo’s 1/6 share to Gregorio, petitioners were able to establish said transaction by parol evidence, consisting of the testimonies of Gregorio Averia, Jr., Veronica Averia and Felimon Dagondon the presentation of which was, it bears repeating, not objected to.
One sentence across pages; names retained as printed.
Such disclaimer cannot, however, prevail over the categorical, positive statements of petitioners’ above-named witnesses.
Current Court weighs Domingo’s denial against witness testimony.
They proved the full performance or execution of the contracts as well.
Current Court conclusion that performance was proved.
WHEREFORE, the petition is hereby GRANTED.
The January 31, 2000 Decision of the Court of Appeals in CA-G.R. No. 44704 is hereby SET ASIDE.
The case is hereby remanded to the trial court, Branch 31 of the RTC of Manila, for appropriate action, following Section 2 of Rule 69 of the Rules of Civil Procedure.
